refnamediv.refpurpose: Save resource snapshots as GMAT script

refsection.title: Output files
refsection.para: By default, FilenameStyle = Worksheet writes each selected resource to ObjectName.ObjectType in the output directory. Each snapshot includes its supported attachment dependencies.

Filename selects an exact output filename and combines the selected objects in that file, overriding the default naming style. Relative filenames use the configured output directory. An empty filename restores default naming. Double an apostrophe inside a quoted filename.

Explicitly selected resources and their serialized owned components are included even when declared in an included file or a function source. The original source-file association remains intact for ordinary script saving.

Snapshots also write writable properties whose current values match their native defaults, including supported empty values. This lets a later snapshot restore those defaults when it follows an earlier nondefault snapshot in the same file.

Resource serialization preserves each class's property ordering and includes additional native properties without changing the live object's ordering metadata. Invalid duplicate or out-of-range property identifiers are reported while preparing the snapshot, before Save opens output files.

Snapshots explicitly clear writable SPICE kernel lists and spacecraft SolveFors before recording their current entries. Empty or shorter later lists therefore replace the corresponding earlier saved lists when the appended snapshots are read as a script. Other list properties retain their own native serialization and setter policies.

ReportFile reported parameters, XYPlot Y variables, and OrbitPlot member lists also receive an explicit empty-list reset before their current entries. Shorter or empty snapshots therefore replace the earlier member lists. XYPlot keeps its X variable while clearing Y members. The reader uses each subscriber's existing native Clear action, including its wrapper and plot-list cleanup; it does not open a report stream to serialize the list.

The same reset-before-entries policy applies to DataFilter FileNames, ObservedObjects, Trackers and DataTypes, SolarPowerSystem ShadowBodies, CelestialBody DSNMediaFileDirectories and ContactLocator EventTypes. Their native setters or clear actions handle explicit empty lists; ordinary list assignments retain their existing behavior. Read-only DataFilter Strands is not reset.

Estimator and Simulator snapshots clear their previous Propagator selection before recording the default and spacecraft-specific mappings. This replaces longer or differently mapped earlier selections in appended snapshots, including an empty selection. The native reset retires the owned propagator definitions and invalidates their prepared satellite map. A later estimator/simulator run must prepare its newly selected definitions; serialization does not reset the live source resource.

Estimator Measurements, AddSolveFor, AddResidualsPlot and DataFilters, and Simulator AddData, also reset before their saved entries. Their native clear operations retire owned measurement/filter/plot definitions and invalidate prepared state roles as needed. Clearing solve-for selections preserves the measurement selection. Declared consider/participant roles and manager service configuration remain available for native preparation; saved declarations do not resume a previous estimation or simulation session. Use an unquoted {} to clear these navigation lists; quoted or encoded strings containing empty braces are rejected before they can clear a selection.

Explicit estimator AddSolveFor declarations stage their selection and associated state-manager role lists before publication. Syntax/index errors caught by these setters do not replace the existing declaration. Native estimation preparation still checks the selected object's property compatibility and scientific domain.

TrackingFileSet snapshots reset AddTrackingConfig, FileName, RampTable, DataFilters and SimTDRSServiceAccessList before their saved entries. Each tracking configuration is written as a separate native configuration statement. Native clears retire generated adapters and relevant owned filters, clear prepared caches and require preparation before further use. Existing native service defaults and file/configuration requirements still apply during preparation.

A raw {} clears a tracking collection. A quoted or encoded filename containing empty braces remains filename data; it does not clear the list. Empty-brace string literals cannot select a tracking configuration or data-filter object.

Navigation and tracking collection resets are handled before a declaration is split into object or string-array tokens. A complete AddTrackingConfig assignment parses its participant and measurement-type tokens into temporary definitions before publication. A rejected token or allocation failure during parsing retains the previous declaration. Direct indexed parser calls retain their accepted incremental prefix; native preparation still checks resource bindings and domains.

A PlanetographicRegion snapshot first clears AreaFileName, Latitude and Longitude, then records its active file or inline input definition. Later snapshots can replace longer coordinate lists or switch between these input modes. Coordinate resets use the native whole-vector setter; serialization does not clear the live source region.

A DynamicDataDisplay snapshot clears its previous layout with AddParameters = {}; before adding rows. Row properties then preserve backgrounds, color modes and warning/critical bounds by cell position, including blank cells and fixed black text. Later snapshots can replace a longer table or restore its default cell settings. These row properties require an updated reader.

Save records finite native Real values with sufficient significant digits to preserve their binary value on reload, independently of a lower display precision. Numeric literals use a decimal point and no locale digit grouping. This includes Variable values, Array cells, common numeric resource properties and saved plot viewpoint vectors. Ordinary script generation retains its configured formatting. Coordinate conversions and other calculated representations retain their native computation rules.

Saved native string and filename properties, quoted string-list entries and String-resource values use an explicit byte literal when ordinary quoting cannot safely represent the value. Its syntax is @'HEX', with two hexadecimal digits per byte. This preserves apostrophes, line breaks, control bytes, Unicode bytes and punctuation that can otherwise be parsed as script structure. Simple values retain their ordinary single-quoted form; backslashes in existing quoted strings retain their literal meaning. An explicitly saved empty String includes its empty assignment, so a later snapshot clears an earlier value.

Encoded literals require a reader supporting this syntax. Native string-property, String-resource and string-argument readers decode them at their input boundary; they always denote string data, including when the decoded value is also a resource name. Existing single-quoted literal interpretation is unchanged. Specialized class serializers, equation text and external-file portability retain their own contracts.
